issues.legal_issue: An appellate or revisional court may entertain an objection to the place of suing only when the objection was raised at the required stages and the wrong choice of venue caused a failure of justice.
material_facts: A partition suit was filed in one court, which issued a preliminary decree; after territorial boundaries changed, an application for a final decree was filed in another court.
A defendant objected to the second court’s territorial jurisdiction immediately, and the objection was raised again on appeal.
The defendant did not identify any failure of justice caused by the choice of the second court, and the record contained no material from which such a failure could be inferred.
The High Court accepted the venue objection and set aside the final decree.
issues.conclusion: The objection could not be entertained by the appellate courts because, although it was raised at the required stages, no consequent failure of justice was shown. The appeal was allowed, the High Court judgment was set aside, and the matter was remanded for decision on the remaining merits; the Court did not decide whether the second court had territorial jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 21(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, an appellate or revisional court may entertain an objection to the place of suing only if the objection was taken in the court of first instance, was taken at the earliest possible opportunity and, where issues are settled, at or before that settlement, and there was a consequent failure of justice. All three conditions must coexist. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: appellate_or_revisional_review_of_venue_objection and venue_objection and objection_raised_in_first_instance and objection_raised_at_earliest_opportunity and not consequent_failure_of_justice

predicates.appellate_or_revisional_review_of_venue_: An appellate or revisional court is reviewing an objection to the place of suing.
predicates.venue_objection: A party objects that the case was brought in the wrong place.
predicates.objection_raised_in_first_instance: The party raised the venue objection in the court of first instance.
predicates.objection_raised_at_earliest_opportunity: The party raised the objection at the earliest opportunity and, when issues were settled, at or before their settlement.
predicates.consequent_failure_of_justice: The wrong choice of venue caused a failure of justice.
predicates.appellate_court_must_not_entertain_venue: The appellate or revisional court does not entertain the venue objection.

issues.definition: When an appellate or revisional court reviews a venue objection that was raised in the first-instance court at the required time, but the wrong venue caused no failure of justice, the court does not entertain the objection.
